Introduction #

Ownership is the idea that every value has exactly one owner, and that the owner decides when the value is dropped. It sounds small, but it changes how APIs are shaped.

Consider a function that takes a String by value. The caller gives up the string, and the compiler checks that it is not used again, which removes a whole class of bugs.

Three rules

  • Each value has one owner.
  • Ownership can move, explicitly.
    • Moves are cheap.
  • When the owner goes, the value is dropped.
fn consume(s: String) {
    println!("{s}");
}

Make illegal states unrepresentable, and the compiler becomes your reviewer, tirelessly, on every build.

Read more in the borrowing post, or the official book, which covers lifetimes, traits, and smart pointers.
